2609.17141.title: Continual Learning for Traversability Prediction with Uncertainty-Aware Adaptation
2609.17141.paper_summary: Traversability prediction is a critical component of autonomous navigation in unstructured environments, where complex and uncertain robot-terrain interactions pose significant challenges such as traction loss and dynamic instability. Despite recent progress in learning-based traversability prediction, these methods often fail to adapt to novel terrains. Even when adaptation is achieved, retaining experience from previously trained environments remains a challenge, a problem known as catastrophic forgetting. To address this challenge, we propose a continual learning framework for traversability prediction that incrementally adapts to new terrains using a generative experience recall model. A key virtue of the proposed framework is two folds: i) retain prior experience without storing past data; and ii) incorporate the uncertainty of the generated samples from the recall model, enabling uncertainty-aware adaptation. Real-world experiments with a skid-steering robot validate the effectiveness of the proposed framework, demonstrating its ability to adapt across a series of diverse environments while mitigating catastrophic forgetting.
2609.17141.paper_summary_zh: 可通行性預測是自主導航在非結構化環境中的關鍵組成部分，因為複雜且不確定的機器人與地形的互動帶來了如牽引力損失和動態不穩定等重大挑戰。儘管近期在基於學習的可通行性預測方面取得了進展，但這些方法通常無法適應新地形。即使在適應成功的情況下，保留從先前訓練環境中獲得的經驗仍然是一個挑戰，這個問題被稱為災難性遺忘。為了解決這一挑戰，我們提出了一個持續學習框架，用於可通行性預測，該框架利用生成經驗回憶模型逐步適應新地形。所提框架的一個主要優點有兩個方面：i) 在不存儲過去數據的情況下保留先前的經驗；以及 ii) 結合來自回憶模型的生成樣本的不確定性，實現不確定性感知的適應。與一個滑轉轉向機器人的實驗驗證了所提框架的有效性，展示了其在一系列多樣化環境中適應的能力，同時減輕了災難性遺忘的影響。
